name: Low-Degree Corners Descend within the Ample Forbidden Basis
statement: Let $H$ be an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction to dismantlable ampleness. If $a$ is a corner of degree at most two, then $H\setminus\{a\}$ is again an irredundantly embedded ample pc-minimal obstruction. Hence, if no corner deletion remains in the ample forbidden basis, every corner has degree at least three.
proof: Corner deletion leaves an ample family $S$, and low-support relative invariance keeps it nonpeelable. A coordinate constant on $S$ would make $S$ a proper signed restriction of $H$ and therefore peelable, so the embedding remains irredundant. Every elementary image of $H$ peels. Its corresponding image of $S$ is either identical or obtained by deleting a concept from an ample extension whose acquired support still has size at most two; low-support invariance therefore makes that image peel as well. Thus every proper pc-minor of $S$ is dismantlable ample.
